author.bio: Thomas Szasz (1920–2012) was a Hungarian-American psychiatrist and longtime professor at SUNY Upstate Medical University. Known for The Myth of Mental Illness, he challenged coercion and the use of psychiatric language as social control; The Second Sin presents his observations in aphoristic form.

context.heading: Why it mattered
lead: The sentence is cited to “Personal Conduct” in Szasz’s The Second Sin. Its three-part structure separates forgiveness from forgetting, rather than treating the two as interchangeable. It belongs to a collection of provocative observations on human conduct, not a clinical instruction about memory or trauma.
